subject.title: fix(line): deliver pre-drain spool rows instead of dead-lettering them on upgrade

question: Should this short-lived shipped LINE queue format be recovered through a one-time Doctor/upgrade migration, or should maintainers explicitly approve a time-bounded runtime compatibility reader for it?
rationale: The repository policy prefers verified migration over persistent fallback readers, but operators can otherwise lose already-acknowledged messages during the upgrade; choosing the user-facing recovery mechanism requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Use a one-time canonical migration
options.body: Migrate matching pre-drain rows before normal drain processing, verify the results, and keep the runtime reader limited to the current payload and ID scheme.

options.title: Approve a temporary runtime bridge
options.body: Retain the reader only with an explicit owner, removal condition, and proof that the bridge cannot admit a changed legacy row into the wrong lane.

recommendation.title: Use a one-time canonical migration
recommendation.body: Migrate matching pre-drain rows before normal drain processing, verify the results, and keep the runtime reader limited to the current payload and ID scheme.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the merged LINE spool and shared-drain transitions that define both persisted formats and the intended upgrade boundary.
